BiblicalUsage: Once, in the taunt of Sanballat, who asks what these feeble Jews think they are doing: will they fortify themselves, will they sacrifice, will they make an end in a day, will they revive the stones out of the heaps of the rubbish which are burned? The word is languid, feeble, and the enemy means it as mockery, that the Jews are too weak to build.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for feeble carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the taunt, that the men called too weak to build finished the wall in fifty-two days.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
